To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a hybrid approach to knowledge representation based on objectoriented and logic programming paradigms is a promising direction for the future development of KR languages (2) the hybrid approach is not only promising in theory but is also supported by a number of practical implementations of the approach (3) a number of non classic logics can be successfully used in KR languages and (4) the use of these logics can be beneficial in some special cases Knowledge representation; Object-oriented; Logic
the following are true: The object oriented approach is a good one for representing knowledge in a way that is close to how people think and talk about the world.

the use of logic programming in the knowledge representation domain is not only a natural and useful extension of the classical approach but also a powerful tool for solving a number of difficult and important problems that are not easily handled in other frameworks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1.

the study of knowledge representation and reasoning in a distributed environment, where the knowledge is stored in several different sites, each of them having its own knowledge base and its own inference engine.
the study of a class of knowledge representation languages which we call object oriented and logic based knowledge representation languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the integration of Object Oriented and Prolog like languages is the best basis for Knowledge Representation in the sense of the classical paradigm of Artificial Intelligence Knowledge Representation and the Integration of Object Oriented Languages and Logic Programming.

Object Oriented and logic based Knowledge Representation systems are a stable basis for the development of Knowledge Representation at the Symbolic level, and that the integration of the Object Oriented and the Logic Programming paradigms in such a context is a particularly fruitful one

the Object Oriented and Logical paradigms are complementary in the Knowledge Representation domain and that a synthesis of the two paradigms provides a powerful basis for the representation of knowledge
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are trying to develop a general theory of knowledge representation and reasoning in a multi agent system which is based on the integration of the logic programming paradigm with the object oriented paradigm We have been working for a number of years on the development of a system called KODIAK which is a multi agent knowledge based system which has a logic programming based inference engine with an object oriented database as its knowledge base The system has been designed with the goal of providing a framework for the representation of knowledge in a multi agent
we are working on a logic programming based language that supports a variety of knowledge representation tasks and has an object oriented syntax
the Object Oriented and the Logic Based approaches are complementary rather than competitive in the field of knowledge representation
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no one single best way to represent knowledge but rather that there are many different approaches that can be used in a complementary manner to represent the same knowledge in different ways and that these different ways are not only useful for representing knowledge in different domains but are also complementary in the sense that they can be used together in the same system to provide different perspectives on the same domain
